chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Marwan, from a number of our companions, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the Sacred Masjid: For what reason did God name it al-Ateeq (the free)? So he said: There is no house that God placed upon the face of the earth except that it has a lord (owner) and dwellers who dwell in it — apart from this House (Kaaba), for there is no lord for it except God, Mighty and Majestic, and it is the Free (al-Hurr).
Then he said: Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, created it before the earth, then He created the earth after it and spread it out from beneath it.

key_terms.الْحُرُّ: al-Hurr — the free one; synonym of al-Ateeq, emphasizing the Kaaba's exclusive divine ownership
key_terms.الْعَتِيق: al-Ateeq — a Quranic name for the Kaaba (Q 22:29, 33), meaning the free/ancient one; the Imam explains it refers to freedom from human ownership
key_terms.دَحَاهَا: spread/extended it — refers to the flattening of the earth from beneath the Kaaba; cf. Q 79:30

ai.seo_question: Why is the Kaaba called al-Ateeq (the free)?
ai.summary: Abu Hamza al-Thumali asked Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) about the Quranic name al-Ateeq (the free/ancient) for the Sacred House (Kaaba). The Imam explained that unlike every other structure on earth which has human owners, the Kaaba belongs exclusively to God, making it truly free. He further revealed a cosmological teaching: the Kaaba was created before the earth itself, and the earth was then spread out from beneath it, establishing the Kaaba as the primordial center of creation.
